Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

peace noun

the absence of war

also make peace, peacetime, at peace, make peace with, break the peace, bring about peace, peace is concluded on condition that, terms of peace, accept terms of peace, dictate terms of peace, propose terms of peace, peace terms

classical

Liv. 30.30.19
Cic. Phil. 2.113
Traupman 187

pāx, pācis f.

noun, third declension

To make peace with someone, pācem facere cum aliquō; to break the peace, pācem frangere; in peace and in war, domī mīlitiaeque (Traupman 187).

Examples

  • melior tūtiorque est certa pāx quam spērāta victōria

    a sure peace is better and safer than a hoped-for victoryLiv. 30.30.19

  • Pāx est tranquilla lībertās

    Peace is liberty at restCic. Phil. 2.113

  • pācem facere cum aliquō

    to make peace with someoneTraupman 187

  • pācem frangere

    to break the peaceTraupman 187

  • pācem conciliāre

    to bring about peaceTraupman 187

  • pāx convēnit in eam condiciōnem ut …

    peace was agreed on condition that …Traupman 187

  • pācis condiciōnēs ferre

    to propose terms of peaceTraupman 188

  • pācis condiciōnēs accipere (repudiāre)

    to accept (reject) terms of peaceTraupman 188

  • pācis condiciōnēs alicui dīcere

    to dictate terms of peace to someoneTraupman 188

  • Suspīciō bonā fidē et mūtuā observantiā substituenda est.

    Suspicion must be replaced by mutual trust and respect.Traupman 185

See also war, peace, victory.
